lesson_yaml:
schema: cairn/lesson/v0.1
id: python-flask-lemur-export-private-key-without-authz
title: Certificate export passes cert.private_key to plugin.export regardless of plugin.requires_key authz
  gate
summary: The export endpoint only performed the ownership/permission check inside the `plugin.requires_key`
  branch, but then always passed `cert.private_key` to `plugin.export`. A plugin that does not declare
  `requires_key` could receive and leak the private key to a user who was never authorized to view it,
  and the key_view audit log was written unconditionally. Key material must only be passed after the authorization
  check and only when the plugin requires it.
cwe:
- CWE-862
- CWE-285
severity: high
confidence: medium
languages:
- python
source:
  kind: fix-commit
  ref: 5683bbea8b10cce07f9a8abf1e4a7d3b2031c585
  vulnerable_ref: 5683bbea8b10cce07f9a8abf1e4a7d3b2031c585^
  patched_ref: 5683bbea8b10cce07f9a8abf1e4a7d3b2031c585
  repository: https://github.com/Netflix/lemur
rule:
  message: '`$CERT.private_key` is passed directly to `$PLUGIN.export(...)`. The authorization check is
    only done when `$PLUGIN.requires_key` is true, so other plugins can receive the private key without
    any permission check. Use a local `private_key` variable that is set only after the authz check inside
    the requires_key branch.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern: $PLUGIN.export($CERT.body, $CERT.chain, $CERT.private_key, $OPTS)
  - pattern-not-inside: "if $PLUGIN.requires_key:\n    ...\n    $PLUGIN.export($CERT.body, $CERT.chain,\
      \ $CERT.private_key, $OPTS)\n"
fix:
  guidance: Initialise `private_key = None` before the check. Inside the `if plugin.requires_key:` block,
    verify the key exists, enforce the CertificatePermission check for non-creators, write the key_view
    audit log, and only then assign `private_key = cert.private_key`. Pass the local `private_key` variable
    to `plugin.export` instead of reading `cert.private_key` directly.
  example: "private_key = None\nif plugin.requires_key:\n    if not cert.private_key:\n        return\
    \ dict(message=\"no key\"), 400\n    if g.current_user != cert.user:\n        permission = CertificatePermission(owner_role,\
    \ [x.name for x in cert.roles])\n        if not permission.can():\n            return dict(message=\"\
    You are not authorized to export this certificate.\"), 403\n    log_service.create(g.current_user,\
    \ \"key_view\", certificate=cert)\n    private_key = cert.private_key\nextension, passphrase, data\
    \ = plugin.export(cert.body, cert.chain, private_key, options)\n"

  vulnerable:
  - fixtures/vulnerable/views.py
  patched:
  - fixtures/patched/views.py

sibling_hits.reason: This service helper passes cert.private_key to plugin.export without checking plugin.requires_key or authorization, which is the lesson's pattern, but the authz check belongs to the calling endpoint and the callers are not shown.
